title: Rejoining Lester in Salina; Bronson's band, a rival and a new alto
summary: Phillips and Pete Jones pawn a suit to go back to Lester, who is shooting pool; Bronson's men were weaker, rival bandleader Ted Williams was jealous, and Bronson brought in Albert Walters on alto.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Before you get into King Oliver, could you tell us a little bit more about Bronson. Exactly when did Lester join, when did he quit, did he ever re-join? All that stuff, if you could tell us about that?
Yeah, well, he quit...
First of all, how did he join?
We all joined Bronson the same time, and we stayed with Bronson until...
Phillips - 78
Salina, Kansas.
We joined him in Salina, Kansas.
Right, in January 1928.
Pete and I, we quit in Wichita, Kansas... We called him Bub. We said, "Man, let's go back where Bub is."
You called Lester Young "Bub."

Bub, yeah. "Let's go back where he is." Pete said, "Okay." Our money was short, we didn't have too much money. So I pawned one of my suits and got enough money for me and Pete to catch the bus to go back where he was. When we got back where he was... You know, in them days, you didn't think about no money or nothin' too much. You know, people was more friendly than they are now. So when we got back there, he said... He was shooting pool. He said, "What are ya'll doin' here, man! Oh, I'm so glad to see you'all." You know what I mean? Because we was, all three of us was tight, together. He said, "There's a guy got a band here said he want to enlarge his band to a 10-piece band. He's got about 6 pieces now." "Yeah?" So this cat talked with Art, and he said... See, them cats, they wasn't playing like we was playing.
The people in Bronson's band.
Yeah, because they hadn't been with the company that we'd been with. You know what I mean? So when
Phillips - 79

he got there... They had another cat had a band around there named Ted Williams or Ted... I think it was Ted Williams. He had a band around there. Man, and they got jealous of Bronson. They were doing everything to try to make things hard for him. But they couldn't do it, because we were blowin' so much. And everybody quit listening to him. So they gave a dance. When they'd give a dance, they'd hear us playing, and in the meantime... I'm a little ahead of my story. We had an alto player that was a Jamaican; he used to play first alto with Mr. Young's band, and then he left and went to Omaha. Then we got to thinking about him, where could Bronson get a good first alto player. He could read like mad and...
What's the alto player's name?
His name was Albert Walters. Well, Bronson sent and got him to play first alto, and then we did have a reed section. We had another boy named Buford Boswell, who was playing third.
What was Lester playing?
Tenor.
He was playing tenor at that time.
Yeah, that's when he started. He went on tenor.
He started playing tenor in Bronson's band.
He started playing tenor again, yeah.
